bib.title: Transfusion: Predict the Next Token and Diffuse Images with One Multi-Modal Model

read.skipped: reference list skimmed; appendix image-sample figure text (captions of generated images) not analysed

question: Can one transformer be trained on text with next-token loss and on continuous image latents with diffusion loss, and scale better than quantising images into discrete tokens?
hypothesis: Keeping images continuous and using a diffusion loss for them, with next-token prediction for text, avoids the quantisation bottleneck and scales better than the Chameleon discrete-token recipe.
contributions: Transfusion recipe: LM loss on text plus diffusion loss on image patches in one transformer over mixed-modality sequences
Controlled scaling comparison with Chameleon up to 7B
Ablations on intra-image bidirectional attention, patch size, linear vs U-Net patch encoders, image noise limiting
7B model on 2T tokens compared with image generation literature, plus image editing fine-tune

method.summary: A single Llama-style transformer processes text tokens (embedding matrices) and VAE latent image patches (linear or U-Net down/up layers) in one sequence delimited by BOI/EOI. Causal attention everywhere, bidirectional within each image; loss = LM loss + 5 x DDPM loss. Models of 0.16B to 7B trained from scratch and compared with Chameleon-recipe baselines using a VQ-VAE.
method.task: joint pretraining on text (next-token) and text-image pairs (diffusion), evaluated on text, captioning and text-to-image

datasets.name: Text corpus (Llama 2)
datasets.size: 2T tokens corpus; 0.5T tokens sampled in most experiments at 1:1 token ratio with images (1T text tokens in the 4.4 run)
datasets.source: Llama 2 tokenizer and corpus (Touvron et al. 2023b)

datasets.name: Shutterstock images and captions
datasets.preprocessing: center-cropped and resized to 256x256; caption first 80% of the time

datasets.name: Large-scale mixture (sec 4.4)
datasets.size: 692M image-caption pairs per epoch, about 5 epochs, ~3.5B pairs, 1T image patches
datasets.source: Shutterstock + 220M public images without people + 80M upsampled Shutterstock images with people + CC12M
datasets.preprocessing: high-aesthetic images upweighted in last 1% of schedule

datasets.name: Eval: Wikipedia, C4, Llama 2 suite, MS-COCO, GenEval
datasets.size: 20M held-out tokens (Wiki, C4); 30k COCO prompts for FID/CLIP (5k in ablations); COCO Karpathy test 5k for CIDEr

models.name: Transfusion
models.architecture: Llama-style transformer (SwiGLU, RoPE), modality-specific embeddings and linear or U-Net patch encoders, causal attention with bidirectional within images

models.name: Chameleon (controlled baseline)
models.architecture: Llama transformer with query-key norm, post-norm, denominator loss; images quantised by VQ-VAE (16,384 codebook)

training.objective: L_Transfusion = L_LM + lambda * L_DDPM, lambda = 5; DDPM noise-prediction MSE, cosine noise schedule, 1,000 training timesteps
training.epochs: about 5 epochs of images in 4.4 run
training.compute: FLOPs proxied as 6ND; no GPU-hours stated

other.VAE loss: L1 + LPIPS + 0.5 GAN + 0.2 ID + 0.000001 KL, GAN from step 50,000
other.timestep embedding: added to every patch vector before linear layer

inference.decoding: text: greedy; images: 250 diffusion steps with classifier-free guidance; LM/diffusion mode switch at BOI
inference.samples: no seeds or repeat runs stated; FID/CLIP on 30k COCO prompts (5k in ablations)
inference.prompting: ranked classification for Llama 2 eval suite (0-shot)

parameters.CFG coefficient: 5 in controlled comparison, 3 in ablations, tuned per benchmark in 7B run

metrics.name: Llama 2 eval suite accuracy
metrics.definition: average 0-shot accuracy on HellaSwag, PIQA, SIQA, WinoGrande, ARC-e/c, BoolQ

metrics.name: FID
metrics.definition: zero-shot, MS-COCO 30k generated images (5k in ablations)

metrics.name: Parity FLOP ratio
metrics.definition: FLOPs Transfusion needs to match Chameleon's performance, divided by Chameleon's, from log-log linear trendlines

baselines: Imagen, Parti, SD 1.5, SD 2.1, DALL-E 2, SDXL, DeepFloyd, SD 3 (reported numbers)
eval.protocol: Scaling points at 5 sizes with linear trendlines on log metric vs log FLOPs; Chameleon points removed below thresholds (FID<=100, CLIP>=17, CIDEr>=4); single runs.

evidence.quote: warmed up for 4000 steps and decaying

results.claim: At 7B in the controlled setup Transfusion reaches Chameleon's FID with 34x less compute.
results.setup: 7B, 0.5T tokens, linear 2x2 patch encoder, bidirectional attention, 256x256 images, CFG 5, MS-COCO 30k
results.quote: FID Transfusion achieves parity with Chameleon using 34× less compute
results.note: Table 3 lists parity FLOP ratio 0.029 for FID

results.claim: Same setup: FID 16.8 for Transfusion versus 29.6 for Chameleon at 7B.
results.table: Table 3, rows Transfusion and Chameleon, column FID (16.8 vs 29.6)

results.claim: Image-to-text: Transfusion matches Chameleon at 21.8% of the FLOPs.
results.quote: Transfusion matches Chameleon at 21.8% of the FLOPs

results.claim: The 7.3B Transfusion model scores 0.63 on GenEval, above SDXL (0.55) and below SD 3 (0.68).
results.setup: 7.3B with U-Net layers, 2x2 patches, 2T tokens (1T text, 3.5B images), CFG tuned per benchmark; SD 3 trained with synthetic captions, baselines are literature numbers
results.table: Table 9, row Transfusion (Ours), column Gen Eval
results.note: Text says SD 3 synthetic captions boost GenEval by 6.5% absolute (0.433->0.498) at smaller scale

results.claim: The 7.3B model has COCO FID 6.78 and Llama-suite accuracy 66.1, equal to Llama 1 (66.1).
results.table: Table 9, row Transfusion (Ours), columns COCO FID and Llama Acc

results.claim: Intra-image bidirectional attention cuts FID from 61.3 to 20.3 with linear encoding.
results.quote: in FID when using linear encoding layers (61.3→20.3)

results.claim: U-Net encoder/decoder lets a 1.4B transformer beat the linear 7B on CIDEr (28.1 vs 27.2) and gives 0.76B FID 16.7 vs 20.3.
results.table: Table 7, rows 1.4B U-Net and 7B Linear, column CDr

results.claim: Larger patches with U-Net compress each image to 16 patches at small cost (FID 16.1 vs 16.7).
results.table: Table 6, rows U-Net 8×8 (16.1) and 2×2 (16.7), column FID

results.claim: Serving cost could drop by up to 64x via larger patches.
results.quote: potentially decreasing the serving costs by up to 64×.

results.claim: On text, Transfusion also beats Chameleon: C4 PPL 7.72 vs 8.41 at 7B.

limits: Single runs with no seeds or confidence intervals stated
lambda=5 and other settings not tuned
Image sizes only 256x256, modalities only text and images
SD3 comparison confounded by synthetic captions; baselines are literature numbers
Reason for text gain over Chameleon left to future work
Image-editing result is manual inspection of examples only
Chameleon baseline includes stability modifications that cost efficiency, so the gap partly reflects recipe differences

terms.definition: the ratio between the number of FLOPs required by Transfusion and Chameleon to reach the same level of performance
